newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE ISLAND
Sri Lanka Railways struggles to maintain services due to lack of locomotives and spare parts.
Trade unions representing teachers oppose moves to reduce number of holidays enjoyed by school teachers.
DAILY NEWS
Gas distribution returns to normal after six-day strike by Shell Gas Lanka employees was settled on Tuesday.
Former army commander Cecil Waidyaratne, remanded for alleged corruption over dry ration packs purchased for the army, is released on bail.
LANKADEEPA
Security forces uncover plan by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) suicide bombers to kill Education Minister Richard Pathirana in goverment-controlled northern Jaffna peninsula.
Security forces in Jaffna recover a cache of 467 hand grenades from toilet.
DINAMINA
Security forces in Colombo placed on red alert to prevent attacks by LTTE guerrillas during their "Heroes' Week" which ends on November 26
Local government elections, postponed three times by the government, to be held in April, deputy minister Jeyaraj Fernandopulle tells parliament.
DIVAINA

Government will take legal action against those harbouring army deserters, Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte says. Amnesty granted for deserters to rejoin their units extended till end of month.
VEERAKESARI
Saracen armoured personnel carrier blown up by rebel mine near Kodikamam in Jaffna while air force fighter jets bomb two LTTE bases in the north.
THINAKARAN
Students in eastern province protest against alleged rape and murder of a Tamil girl by soldiers in Jaffna.
Fomer rebel group Eelam People's Revolutionary Liberation Front (EPRLF) members meet Indian opposition Bharathiya Janatha Party (BJP) leaders in Delhi for talks on Sri Lanka's ethnic war.
-- Colombo newsroom 941-434319
